'''''Potamogeton natans''''', commonly known as '''broad-leaved pondweed''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007|access-date=2014-10-17}}</ref> '''floating pondweed''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=PONA4|taxon=Potamogeton natans|access-date=13 October 2015}}</ref> or '''floating-leaf pondweed''', is an aquatic species in the genus ''[[Potamogeton]]'' native to quiet or slow-flowing freshwater habitats throughout the [[Holarctic Kingdom]].

==Description==
[[File:PotamogetonNatans2.jpg|thumb|left|Floating leaves]]
It produces both floating and submersed leaves on the same plant. The floating leaves are [[Glossary of leaf morphology#ovate|ovate]] to oblong-ovate and almost always [[Cordate (leaf shape)|cordate]] at the base. They are dark green, leathery, opaque, with translucent longitudinal veins. They are 5 to 10 cm long, pointed at the tips, and rounded at the base.

The [[stipule]]s are 4 to 17 cm long.

The submerged grass-like structures are called [[phyllode]]s, are actually modified leaf stalks.

The stems are cylindrical, without many branches, and grow from 1 to 2 metres.

The main difference between this species and other [[Potamogeton|pondweeds]] is a discoloured flexible joint just below the top of the long leaf stalk.

The flower spikes are dense, and cylindrical. They are 5 to 10 cm long, pointed at the tip and rounded at the base. It flowers from May to September.

The fruits are 4 to 5 mm long and [[obovate]].<ref name="The Wild Flower Key">{{cite book |last=Rose |first=Francis|author-link=Francis Rose  |title=The Wild Flower Key |year=2006 |publisher=Frederick Warne & Co|isbn=978-0-7232-5175-0 |pages=490–491}}</ref>
